subject: Production: unexpected latency + hallucination after q-profile rollout
messages:
From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@peregrine-sys.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: tom.liu@peregrine-sys.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Production: increased API latency and hallucination after q-profile rollout

Chloe —

We pushed the q-profile v2a last night (2027-09-29 23:50 PDT) and within the first hour we saw a jump in p95 latency from ~180ms to ~520ms for our /generate calls. In addition several recently successful prompts are now returning unrelated entities (hallucinations) ~4-6% of the time.

Samples and logs attached (logs_20270930.zip, sample_responses_20270930.json). This is hitting our checkout flow and causing outages. Can you confirm whether Redwood rolled any model or q-profile changes on our route? We need an ETA on mitigation.

— Ava
Ava Collins
Head of Engineering, Peregrine Systems

From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@peregrine-sys.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: increased API latency and hallucination after q-profile rollout

Ava —

Thank you for the report and the samples. I'm escalating immediately. Initial read: there was a targeted q-profile rollout (v2a) to a subset of routes yesterday evening as part of the quant profiles experiment. I have looped in Ben (runtime) and Irene (SRE) to triage.

Immediate next steps:
- Open triage call in 15 minutes (I'll send invite).
- Ben will look at kernel selection / seq-length hot paths; Irene will check routing and recent binpack changes.
- If we confirm v2a is the cause we'll revert to the prior profile for your route and spin up dedicated fallbacks.

We will update every 30 minutes until stable. Sorry for the disruption — we're on it.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Ava Collins <ava.collins@peregrine-sys.com>, tom.liu@peregrine-sys.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 01:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Production: increased API latency and hallucination after q-profile rollout

On Thu, Sep 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ava Collins <ava.collins@peregrine-sys.com> wrote:
> Chloe —
>
> We pushed the q-profile v2a last night ...

Quick summary of what I found from the perf dump and token profiles attached:
- q-profile v2a (deployed 2027-09-29 23:50 PDT) changes kernel selection heuristics for 32-96 token ranges to use an int8 path that is latency-optimized for long sequences but, with our customer's sequence distribution, triggers additional memory copies on the attention backend. Result: p95 regression for medium-length payloads.
- The hallucination increase looks correlated with quant rounding under v2a for a small subset of embeddings — the model logits are slightly biased on some tokens post-quant; this is visible in token_profile_1001.txt.
- Flamegraph shows a 2.4x increase in attention kernel time for the affected shards (flamegraph_1001.png).

Proposed mitigation (fastest -> safest):
1) Revert q-profile for Peregrine route to v1 (immediate) — ~5-7 minute rollback.
2) If rollback is insufficient, route Peregrine to dedicated instances with v1 pinned.
3) Post-mortem: run a narrow AB test of v2a with token distributions matching Peregrine's workload and add a fallback rule in SmartRouting.

I kicked off a rollback in staging; asking SRE to approve immediate production rollback.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: flamegraph_1001.png, token_profile_1001.txt

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 01:25:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Production: increased API latency and hallucination after q-profile rollout

Rolling back now. Notes for operations:
- Rolling back q-profile on the Peregrine route (route_id: rp-448) at 01:28 UTC. Estimated completion 01:35 UTC.
- We will also enable a temporary SmartRouting rule to route 100% of traffic for rp-448 to v1 for the next 12 hours.
- Spinning up two extra dedicated workers pinned to v1 for a 30m warm window to catch any backlog.

Marissa — need quick approval for a one-off credit / SLA exception if Peregrine requests compensation. Also need your call on a short customer-facing explanation vs. a terse ops update.

Irene Choi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@peregrine-sys.com>, chloe_martin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 02:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Production: increased API latency and hallucination after q-profile rollout

Ava —

I'm very sorry for the interruption — this should not have impacted your checkout flow. We have rolled back the q-profile change for your account and enabled a routed fallback to the previous profile. Irene confirmed the rollback is in progress and Ben's analysis indicates the root cause is a quantization/attention interaction for your workload.

Immediate customer-facing actions:
- We will monitor your p95 and hallucination rate for 24 hours and send a summary at 6h and 24h.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call today with our runtime leads to walk through the findings and next steps.
- If this event caused measurable customer impact for you, we'll discuss compensation — I'm authorizing preliminary review for a one-off credit pending the post-mortem.

Again, apologies. We'll keep you updated.

— Marissa Cole
VP Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@peregrine-sys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 18:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Production: increased API latency and hallucination after q-profile rollout — rollback complete

Ava —

Quick update: rollback completed at 01:34 UTC on 2027-10-01. We saw p95 return to baseline within 10 minutes and hallucination rate drop to pre-rollout levels on our sampled prompt set. We will continue to monitor and will share the 6h and 24h reports to this thread.

Attachments: logs_20270930.zip (original), sample_responses_20270930.json (samples we used to validate).

Please let me know if you'd like the technical call this afternoon (PST) or tomorrow.

Thanks for your patience — Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
